html:
Urga was the city that became Ulaanbaatar, the capital of Mongolia. It began in 1639 as a moving camp of tent temples around Zanabazar, the first Jebtsundamba Khutuktu, the head of Buddhism among the Khalkha Mongols. The camp moved some 29 times before it settled for good on the Tuul River in 1778.

Mongols called it Ikh Khüree, "great camp"; Russians called it Urga, from örgöö, a palace tent. It grew into Mongolia's religious centre, home to thousands of monks, and a trading town where Chinese and Russian merchants met on the tea route between China and Kyakhta. In 1911 the eighth Jebtsundamba was enthroned here as Bogd Khan of an independent Mongolia.

After the revolution of 1921 led by Sükhbaatar, the city was renamed Ulaanbaatar, "red hero", in 1924. A Soviet style city replaced most of the temples, though Gandan monastery survived. Today nearly half of Mongolia's people live there, and it is the coldest capital in the world.
